kept.claim: Without a re-check of entryPointAssetsCache after Lock(), concurrent cold-start requests each re-read and re-parse assets-manifest.json in turn instead of reusing the first successful load.
kept.body:
## [OPTIMIZATION] Missing re-check after upgrading to the write lock

**Severity:** LOW - redundant, serialized manifest reads on cold start; not a correctness bug.

### The Problem

```go
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.RLock()
ret := entryPointAssetsCache
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.RUnlock()

if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && ret != nil {
    return ret, nil
}
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()
defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()
// ... always re-reads the file
```

Between `RUnlock()` (line 43) and `Lock()` (line 48) another goroutine may already have filled `entryPointAssetsCache`. Nothing checks it again after line 49. So every goroutine that saw `nil` on the fast path queues on the exclusive lock, then opens, decodes and post-processes `assets-manifest.json` again, one at a time.

### Theory / Proof

`sync.RWMutex` cannot atomically upgrade a read lock to a write lock. The usual Go pattern is double-checked locking: check under `RLock`, then check again under `Lock`. Without the second check the mutex removes the data race, but every caller that missed the fast path still does the full load.

### What happens today vs. what will break

- Warm cache (production): the fast path returns, so there is no cost.
- Cold start: N concurrent first requests to `/` (`pkg/api/index.go:82`) or `/api/frontend/settings` (`pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:62`) do N serialized reads of the manifest where one would do. This is a one-time startup cost. Before this PR those reads happened in parallel, and raced.
- The Dev path deliberately bypasses the cache, so any re-check must keep the `cfg.Env != setting.Dev` condition.

### Research

`sync.OnceValues` (Go 1.21) and `golang.org/x/sync/singleflight` are the standard tools for "compute once, share the result". Double-checked locking with `RWMutex` is the manual equivalent.

### Recommendation

```go
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()
defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()

if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil {
    return entryPointAssetsCache, nil
}
```
kept.evidence: webassets.go:41-49: the re-check is missing, so cold-start callers that missed the fast path each reload in turn. The failure-path half of the original claim was dropped: failures store nil (line 69), so a re-check would not avoid those reloads, and a missing file makes os.Open fail fast. The only caller that matters is page load (index.go:82, frontendsettings.go:62), and the cost is once at startup.

kept.claim: The PR fixes a data race but adds no concurrent test, so nothing under `go test -race` guards against the race coming back.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] No regression test for the data race

**Severity:** LOW - the fix is not protected by a test.

### The Problem

The PR adds `entryPointAssetsCacheMu` to guard `entryPointAssetsCache`, but `pkg/api/webassets/webassets_test.go` only tests `readWebAssetsFromFile` and `SetContentDeliveryURL`. No test calls `GetWebAssets` from more than one goroutine.

### Theory / Proof

The Go race detector only reports races on memory accesses that actually happen during a run. If no test calls `GetWebAssets` concurrently, `go test -race` cannot see a regression, for example someone adding a fast path that reads `entryPointAssetsCache` without the lock.

### Recommendation

```go
func TestGetWebAssetsConcurrent(t *testing.T) {
    cfg := setting.NewCfg()
    cfg.StaticRootPath = t.TempDir()
    // write testdata/sample-assets-manifest.json to <root>/build/assets-manifest.json
    var wg sync.WaitGroup
    for i := 0; i < 20; i++ {
        wg.Add(1)
        go func() { defer wg.Done(); _, _ = GetWebAssets(context.Background(), cfg, &licensing.OSSLicensingService{}) }()
    }
    wg.Wait()
}
```
kept.evidence: webassets_test.go only has TestReadWebassets (line 11) and TestReadWebassetsFromCDN (line 89), and neither calls GetWebAssets. No test in pkg/api or pkg/middleware calls it concurrently: there is no t.Parallel(), and login_test.go stubs setIndexViewData. So -race cannot catch a regression.
